C1.worst_defect: The hero says what it is and offers two clear buttons, but nothing on the home page says who should not pick it or how it compares with what a Vendure shop would otherwise use (a hosted POS such as Shopify POS or Square, or no POS). A buyer has to assemble 'not for you if…' from the scattered 'Before you start' bullets: Postgres only, desktop Chrome tested, no drawer, no coupons.
C1.where: home.desktop.01 hero and home.desktop.02 'Before you start'

C2.worst_defect: The headline and footer say 'open-source' and 'MIT licensed', yet 'To build and host it yourself instead of using app.vendurepos.com, you need your own RxDB Premium licence token (RXDB_PREMIUM)'. A commercial dependency gates self-hosting. The site never says what that licence costs, never names who runs app.vendurepos.com, and gives no support contact or maintainer. The only hint at an owner is an unexplained ph.wcpos.com in the comparison table.
C2.where: home.desktop.02 'Before you start' bullet 5 and the 'Sales reach Vendure' table row; connect-a-till.desktop.01 'Where requests go'

C3.worst_defect: Troubleshooting says the plugin-missing notice clears when 'The store must advertise order.create v4 and register v1, as every plugin release from 0.1.0 does' (the quick start's step 9 says the same). But At the till says 'Charges need plugin 0.3.0' and Notifications says an old plugin holds back 'fee and shipping charges'. A store on 0.1.0 or 0.2.0 passes the stated check and silently loses Add charge, with no troubleshooting line that says why.
C3.where: troubleshooting.txt 'Store settings'; quick-start.desktop.04 step 9; at-the-till.desktop.01 'Add a charge'

C4.worst_defect: The only Changelog covers 'Released versions of the @vendurepos/plugin package'. The till app at app.vendurepos.com, which is most of the product and changes underneath users, has no release history. The plugin entries are written in internal protocol terms ('order.create v5', 'ADR 0005', 'maxShippingLines: 1') rather than what changed for a shop.

C5.worst_defect: The hero product screenshot is cut through a fourth row of product tiles at its bottom edge, so it reads as a clipped capture rather than a framed shot. The docs sidebar also lists 'Quick start' twice: once in the top group (Docs / Live demo / Quick start) and again under Overview.
C5.where: home.desktop.01 bottom of the hero image (y≈1140); docs.desktop.01 sidebar

C6.worst_defect: On the phone, the hero till screenshot shows its cart column header truncated to 'Q...' beside ITEM and TOTAL, so the first product image a phone visitor sees looks like a broken layout. Pages themselves have no overflow (scrollWidth 390 on every page).
C6.where: home.phone.01 hero image, cart table header

C7.worst_defect: Every sitemap <lastmod> is a build timestamp from 17 to 18 Nov 2026 rather than a content date. For example, /docs/changelog carries lastmod 2026-11-18T12:36:54 although its newest entry is 2026-10-06. Lighthouse is 98/100/100/100, and llms.txt, the search API, the OG card and JSON-LD are all fine.

overall_worst.defect: The site sells VendurePOS as 'open-source' and 'MIT licensed', but self-hosting the till needs a paid RxDB Premium licence at a cost never stated. Otherwise a shop depends on app.vendurepos.com, whose operator, support channel and continuity are never named. A sceptic would advise a client that the open-source claim does not buy independence.
overall_worst.where: home.desktop.02 'Before you start' bullet 5; limitations.desktop.01 bullet 3; connect-a-till.desktop.01
overall_worst.fix: Add a short 'Who runs this and what self-hosting costs' block to the home page and Limitations. It should name the maintainer and a support contact, give the RxDB Premium price or a link to it, and say what happens to tills if app.vendurepos.com goes away.
